extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and their institutional grants administrators (postdocs, early-stage investigators, R01/K99/F31/F32 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based guidance and standards for navigating NIH review, administrative processing, and award setup (e.g., eRA statuses, JIT, pre-award spending, PO/GMS interactions, paylines, MPI/ESI implications). Useful for applicants waiting on funding or preparing resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award spending allowance (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can begin pre-award spending, which is allowable up to 90 days before the award starts (true for all awards, not just K99).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your institution must set up a pre-award spending account to charge costs to the award as soon as it is issued. Pre-award spending typically allows hiring, ordering supplies, etc. You cannot retroactively charge past months before the award was active; pre-award spending spreads initial funds forward (see borrowing institution guidance). If institution sets up account you may obtain the higher salary for the first active month but cannot recover months lost prior to award issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Award (NOA) timing after 'Award Prepared' (~7 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is often a delay of about seven days from 'Award prepared' to Notice of Award because ICs provide short notice (Congress-related) and leadership sign-offs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The length between 'Award prepared' and NOA can be as little as hours or a week or more depending on backlog at the IC Director's office; signatures are usually routine. Expect variability and occasional longer waits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meanings of eRA status terms (Pending, Award prepared, Pending administrative review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different eRA Commons status labels indicate different stages: 'Pending' means someone is working with your application; 'Award prepared' usually means Grants Management Specialist prepared the award; 'Pending administrative review' indicates administrative processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status labels can vary across K/R/FP mechanisms and ICs; sometimes applications temporarily move to 'Pending' for minor checks. Do not over-interpret small status wording changes—use them as broad signals and follow up with the appropriate staff when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final funding authority is the IC Director
rubrics_metrics.description: The IC Director has ultimate authority to approve and sign awards; program officials do not issue NOAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delays between 'Award prepared' and NOA often reflect waiting for IC Director sign-off. Program Officers (POs) can advise and advocate but cannot guarantee funding; the IC Director's approval is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on contacting Program Officers (POs)
rubrics_metrics.description: POs are the primary program contacts for scientific/procedural questions and for advice after summary statements, but they are not in the administrative award processing loop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep communication measured—follow up if you haven't heard back for >1 month. Ask POs for resubmission advice after you receive your summary statement. Understand POs cannot promise awards and may be cautious in discussing likelihoods.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to contact SRO, GMS, Branch Chief/Division Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Different roles handle distinct functions: the Scientific Review Officer (SRO) for study section/IRG procedural questions; Grants Management Specialist (GMS) for administrative award prep; Branch Chief/Division Director if PO is unresponsive or for IC-assignment concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If scores/status suggest a meeting glitch or deferral contact the SRO after allowing a few days. For administrative/set-up queries (e.g., award prepared steps, pre-award accounts) contact GMS. If an IC assignment changed unexpectedly or the PO is unhelpful, contact the Branch Chief or Division Director for explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT (Just-in-Time) submission strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of a JIT request is not unusual; you can submit JIT materials proactively so they are available when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting JIT early does not typically affect award timing and can speed administrative processing if IC requests arise. If unsure, have materials ready to submit immediately upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start dates are flexible and can be delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominal start dates are not fixed — they provide guidance and can be delayed by federal budget timing, appropriation arrival, administrative issues, or if regulatory approvals are pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cycle start dates (e.g., Dec 1, Apr 1) can shift based on appropriation timing; if you need coverage because of delays, consult your mentor/department about bridge funding or extension of appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships and small awards often have more favorable payline handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Because fellowships are small and short-term they may be funded at higher percentiles compared with larger grants (R01s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payline behavior varies by IC; consult your PO for context and compare with similar-sized IC paylines. Resubmission improvements in score are weighed by POs and can materially improve funding chances for fellowships (which do not go to Council in some cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Select pay awards frequently incur budget/period cuts; scope change rules
rubrics_metrics.description: ICs sometimes fund 'select pay' awards with reduced budgets and shortened periods (e.g., 20% cut and 1 year shorter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget cuts are common when ICs stretch funds; if the cut is 25% or more you can automatically change the scope of work. For smaller cuts you must request a scope change. Cuts affect future renewals (renewal constrained by current reduced budget), so ask PO about options and consider negotiating scope if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: MPI (multiple-PI) implications for Early Stage Investigators (ESIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying as an MPI with an established investigator can disadvantage an ESI; ESIs may lose ESI-specific advantages (payline, budget) when included as an MPI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ESIs are often better served applying as sole PI to preserve ESI status benefits. Discuss strategy with mentors and POs before submitting MPI proposals if you are an ESI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use eRA Commons and NIH Reporter for tracking timelines/status
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools such as eRA Commons and NIH RePORTER (Approved By date) can help track award approvals and typical timing relative to start dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review others' timelines posted by users for benchmarking; expect variability across cycles and ICs. 'Approved By' dates on RePORTER often indicate awards are issued close to start dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unexpected IC assignment changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application’s IC assignment changes (especially right before review) this can affect interest and funding prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the original PO and/or Branch Chief for clarification. If both POs agree, an application could sometimes be transferred back to the original IC. Ask for explanation but avoid discussing score or funding likelihood prematurely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting summary statements and resubmission advice
rubrics_metrics.description: A positive but out-of-payline score should be addressed via resubmission guided by the summary statement; if criticisms point to clear fixes, resubmit with focused revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the summary statement does not give clear direction (borderline scores with few criticisms), consult the PO for resubmission strategy. When in doubt, plan to revise and resubmit to improve chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up frequency guidance with PO/GMS
rubrics_metrics.description: Regular contact is useful, but over-contacting is discouraged; follow up after a reasonable waiting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical rule used by contributors: follow up if you haven't heard back for >1 month. POs and GMS staff are often busy—time your queries thoughtfully and include clear, concise questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retroactive charging of salary before award active
rubrics_metrics.description: You cannot retroactively charge salary for months before the award was active even if the award later starts; lost increased salary months cannot be recovered from the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may cover missed months out of other funds as a goodwill gesture, but NIH awards cannot pay for costs incurred before the award period. Pre-award spending can cover activities occurring within the 90-day window before the award start date only if institution establishes the account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-award spending mechanics (institution borrows funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-award spending involves the institution fronting money until the award is active — effectively borrowing from the school and later charging the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This spreads the first 12 months of the award over ~12.5–13 months. Discuss details with your institution's grants office (they set up accounts and manage charges). Pre-award spending requires institutional willingness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative delays do not necessarily reflect application quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Long administrative or processing delays (e.g., months in Pending) are often due to workload, federal budget delays, or IC backlogs—not the scientific merit of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain measured communication with PO/GMS, prepare requested documents promptly, and plan contingencies (e.g., bridge funding) rather than assuming a poor review outcome based solely on administrative delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: If score is within funding range, funding decisions may still be delayed to fiscal timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications scored 'within the funding range' can still await final decisions pending IC budget allocations, council actions, or cycle timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICs may not post further eRA updates for months (e.g., until Sep 30) depending on workload and special initiatives; continue preparing but seek institutional contingency plans if job end-dates are near.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRO glitch or deferred review handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If your eRA status stalls at 'Pending IRG Review' or similar after a review date, it may be a closing glitch or deferral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wait a few days; if nothing changes by Friday contact the SRO to confirm whether the application was deferred or the score/summary will post imminently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship score context and IC-specific paylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Paylines for fellowships and NRSA awards vary substantially across ICs (examples: NHLBI F31/32 ~39th percentile, NICHD ~22nd percentile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare your score to the specific IC's recent behavior and consult the PO. Large improvements on resubmission are considered positively and can influence funding despite nominal percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PO advocacy and limits on promises
rubrics_metrics.description: POs may indicate optimism but cannot guarantee awards; nothing is official until NOA is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PO feedback for strategy (resubmission, transfers, budget negotiations) but do not rely on oral assurances for planning career moves; secure departmental support or bridge funding when necessary.
